stem: At what age does the femoral head typically begin to ossify in an infant?
explanation: The ossification process of the femoral head generally starts during this window, making earlier X-rays less effective.
rationale: This timing explains why ultrasound is preferred over X-ray in very young infants.

optionExplanations.A: At birth, the hip joint structures are largely cartilaginous and do not yet show significant bone formation.
optionExplanations.B: The ossification process of the femoral head generally starts during this window, making earlier X-rays less effective.
optionExplanations.C: By this age, ossification is usually well underway; however, the process starts earlier in typical development.
optionExplanations.D: Ossification begins much earlier than the one-year mark, though late presentation of DDH can affect the size of the ossification center.
